family_scale1__Z_00428_2.desc: A wider badge-style tag with a rounded rectangular body, two small rivet holes along one edge, a keyhole slot near the top, and a debossed logo panel in the middle; the corners are broadly rounded and one short edge is hemmed for stiffness.

family_scale1__Z_00198_1.desc: Wider same-family bracket with two parallel vertical webs connected by a top rail, a single central gusset, and lightening pockets milled into the base between the ribs; the webs use slotted mounting holes while the base carries a staggered six-hole clearance pattern and a counterbored locating boss.

family_scale1__Z_00588_1.desc: A short internally splined coupling hub with an integral radial mounting flange at one end and a pilot counterbore at the other. A single row of coarse internal splines sits between a snap-ring groove and a replaceable wear sleeve, while the flange face adds a central keyway and six blind tapped holes and two cross-drilled lubrication holes pierce the wall.

family_scale1__Z_00284_1.desc: A deeper open caddy of the same molded-tray family with a reinforced rim and two integral dividers making three lengthwise bays. One bay uses a regular grid of small circular locator holes, another has cross ribs beneath the floor for stiffness, and the outer corners are rounded with small underside feet.

family_scale1__Z_00635_1.part_family: slender multi-slot extruded aluminium profile rail
family_scale1__Z_00635_1.desc: A similar extruded rail but with one open T-slot centred on each of four faces and a single central bore sized for an end tap. The ends are left square and unchamfered, and a pair of cross-drilled holes near one end accepts a separate mounting bracket.

family_pilot__Z_00048_1.desc: A split cradle built as two mating half shells, a lower seat and an upper strap, each with two side ears carrying through bolt holes so the round bore closes into a complete ring. The outer back of the lower half has one transverse stiffening rib and generous fillets where the ears blend into the shell.

family_scale1__Z_00666_0.desc: A flat, uniform-thickness ladder rail: a straight upper chord ties a repeating row of rounded teardrop and oval windows, with short necks between cells and generous fillets at every junction. Small round through holes sit at the chord nodes and loop bases, and one end is gathered into a compact two-pin connector while the other end continues the same node pattern.

family_scale1__Z_00503_1.part_family: open rectangular frame of thin channel rails
family_scale1__Z_00503_1.desc: A same-family bezel formed as one continuous rounded-corner loop of channel rail rather than separate straight rails, with a thin sheet closing the opening into a shallow tray. A row of identical counterbored mounting holes is patterned along the longer sides, small standoff bosses sit on the back face, and the inner groove is replaced by a smooth sealing lip with generous corner fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00816_1.part_family: slender thin-wall tubular probe / needle shaft
family_scale1__Z_00816_1.desc: Same-family tube but closed at one end: the tip is spun to a smooth closed dome with a short reduced neck just behind it, while the opposite end is opened into a small rolled mounting flange. A lone lateral port is placed in the constant-section region rather than at the tip, leaving the rest of the wall plain.

family_scale1__Z_00799_0.desc: Thin flat rectangular panel built as one continuous peripheral frame filled with a regular grid of small rectangular through-cells formed by intersecting transverse and longitudinal ribs; both ends terminate in angled pointed (chevron) flanges, and a single solid rectangular raised pad is centred on one face as a contact or boss. Wall and rib thickness are uniform, the cell pattern passes through the panel, and there are no round holes.

family_scale1__Z_00448_0.desc: Thin-walled cylindrical socket with a central through bore and a clustered pattern of radial cross-drilled holes around its mid-length blends through a tapered multifaceted neck into a hollow rectangular box; the box walls carry longitudinal rows of small through holes, a central rectangular window on each side, and a pair of cross-pin holes near the stepped shoulder, with fillets easing the round-to-square transition.

family_scale1__Z_00456_0.desc: A single thin square plate whose flat central web carries a regular eleven-by-eleven array of small through perforations, with four larger through mounting holes set on one common bolt circle toward the corners. The perforated web is bordered by a slightly thicker integral picture-frame rim that raises the edges into a shallow tray, the rim and web being one continuous piece with rounded outside corners and small fillets where the rim meets the face.

family_pilot__Z_00046_0.part_family: thin triangular spacer plate with raised circular pad
family_pilot__Z_00046_0.desc: One-piece flat equilateral triangular panel with a single solid circular boss raised from its top face at the inscribed center and tangent to all three edges. The step from the low panel to the flat pad top is abrupt, the underside is plain, and there are no holes, slots, ribs, or corner rounds.

family_scale1__Z_00214_2.desc: A symmetrical lidless tray with four equal square pockets in a two-by-two grid, linked by low webs so the bays open into one another near the top. A continuous raised outer lip stiffens the rim, two opposed mounting ears each take a single large through hole, a central round boss anchors the middle, and the pocket floors carry small vent slots over a ribbed underside lattice.

family_scale1__Z_00267_1.desc: A D-shaped skeletonized plate of the same constant-thickness family: one long straight edge is a mounting flange carrying an in-line row of clearance holes plus one elongated adjustment slot, while the opposite rounded end wraps a single large through bore. Triangular piercings radiate from the bore toward the flange, leaving three tapered ribs, two flange holes are countersunk, and every transition is radiused.

family_scale1__Z_00280_2.desc: Round fan-guard cover made from a thick outer mounting ring with four radial ears. Concentric circular ribs tied together by straight spokes form a protective grille across the central bore, the hub carries a cluster of tiny through slots, and all outer edges are lightly filleted for safe handling.

family_scale1__Z_00033_2.desc: Compact pressed scissor hinge for a fold-out step: nested flat links ride on raised pivot bosses, include three detent windows and a central anti-rattle rib, and terminate in one wide mounting foot with countersunk holes rather than D-section end caps.

family_scale1__Z_00792_1.desc: A similar formed instrument jaw using one spoon-shaped lower jaw opposed by one forked upper jaw, both driven from a short rectangular tail and a pinned clevis. Shift the pattern to a single pivot bore, one elongated pull-rod slot, several small rivet holes, two stamped stiffening beads, and serrated gripping faces instead of long separated tines.

family_scale1__Z_00522_2.desc: Closed C-shaped clamp variant: a nearly circular thin-walled ring split on one side, with two outward mounting ears at the gap, each ear drilled with a through-hole. Short radial ribs bridge the inner face of the ring, a series of oriented slots is evenly spaced around the arc, and one ear extends into a thumb tab for hand opening.

family_scale1__Z_00600_2.desc: A tapered four-face lattice mast welded from round tube, with four main chords converging from a square root to a small tip and Warren diagonals lacing every face. A thick rectangular base frame with corner bolt-hole pads and internal gussets closes the root, intermediate horizontal ring diaphragms stiffen several bays, and the tip terminates in a clevis lug with a single cross-pin hole.

family_scale1__Z_00108_1.desc: A deeper square enclosure half with a solid, unslotted floor; ventilation is instead provided by a dense field of small circular holes on one face. Two opposite walls carry snap-fit latching hooks and a stepped split line, while the other walls have semicircular cable notches, and threaded-insert bosses sit at the four corners with a continuous internal rib ringing the base.

family_scale1__Z_00717_0.part_family: stamped and formed slotted thin-metal carrier strip
family_scale1__Z_00717_0.desc: A long, straight, slender carrier built as a uniform thin-walled metal strip with a near-closed small rectangular profile and plain cut ends. Its faces are densely punched in a repeating layout: many tiny rounded-corner piercings, seven short obround slots in each of two side-wall runs, and on the top face two spaced groups of three longer obround slots set among small round holes on a regular pitch, with every punched corner finished by a small fillet.

family_scale1__Z_00151_1.desc: A related spoked disc uses a thicker keyed hub with six tapered arms into an outer flange; perimeter paddles are omitted and replaced by a bolt circle of through holes plus scalloped lightening pockets, with broad filleted spokes.

family_scale1__Z_00074_0.desc: This part is an elongated injection-moulded insulating header: a straight top rail carries three in-line cylindrical contact sockets whose bores open upward, the two end barrels being taller chimney bosses tied together by webbed segments and a notched central bridge. One broad face is built up as a thin ribbed bulkhead, and three long parallel blade terminals extend far out of the body; counterbored recesses, angled lead-in chamfers around the sockets, small through slots and stiffening side ribs complete the shell.

family_scale1__Z_00120_1.desc: A same-family etched aperture plate laid out as a flat annular disc with six round ports on a bolt circle around a larger clear central window; there are no raised cups, only etched openings. One outer edge is a toothed gear arc for a drive pinion while the opposite side provides two locating-pin bores, a radial alignment slot and two integral spring fingers, with lightening slots between the ports and radiused slot and tooth roots.

family_scale1__Z_00128_2.part_family: thin molded spoke-and-ring protective grille (fan/vent guard)
family_scale1__Z_00128_2.desc: Shallow domed cover grille of the same family: a dished thin shell is perforated by many small round holes in a polar pattern and ends in a rolled outer flange that press-fits into a bezel. Three equally spaced bayonet tabs on the underside provide the retention, and an embossed ring near the rim replaces any central mounting hole.

family_scale1__Z_00153_1.part_family: ribbed molded enclosure cover with hinge lug
family_scale1__Z_00153_1.desc: A lid of the same molded-cover family but with the hinge replaced by two separate short pivot ears on the long edge and a snap ridge running around the inner ledge instead of a deep recess. The raised field carries a row of narrow ventilation slots, ribs are concentrated only at the corners, and the hold-down points are moved to molded corner ears with clearance holes.

family_scale1__Z_00684_1.part_family: lightweight lattice-ribbed twin-cheek bearing bracket (joint yoke)
family_scale1__Z_00684_1.desc: Single-cheek variant of the same family: one flat rib-stiffened plate rather than a paired yoke, carrying three collinear stepped bearing bores along its upper edge and a bolted mounting foot along the bottom. Lightening is a honeycomb of hexagonal pockets instead of triangular truss ribs, two elongated slots replace the saddle for pass-through, corners are generously radiused rather than chamfered, and only the bore bosses get large fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00504_2.desc: Closed-ring variant rolled into a near-complete circle: the same thin notched wall is wrapped so the hooked ends meet in an overlapping lap joint, with four evenly spaced through holes around the rim. Short radial fins point inward on the concave face while the convex face remains a smooth continuous skin, and a uniform row of tiny notches forms a flexible bending segment in place of an open toothed foot.

family_pilot__Z_00048_0.desc: A short open cylindrical saddle shell: one thick curved wall wrapping a little more than half of a circle, with a round through-bore along the axis concentric with the outer cylindrical face and a constant wall between them. The crown is cut away to leave a wide upward opening bounded by two straight longitudinal lips, both axial ends are plain square faces, and the part is symmetric about the vertical center plane with no ribs, bosses, or fastener holes.

family_scale1__Z_00437_2.part_family: flat profiled pendant tag with eyelet
family_scale1__Z_00437_2.desc: A symmetrical flat charm blank shaped as a five-point star with a small circular loop on the top point and one through bore. Two weight-relief holes sit in the inner points, the rim is scalloped, and all features lie in one constant-thickness sheet with no bosses.

family_scale1__Z_00361_2.desc: An annular tube-sheet variant is a flat donut-shaped plate with a keyed central opening, an inner ring of larger through bores each having a one-sided raised hub, an outer bolt circle of small clearance holes, and short radial ribs tying several hubs to the outer rim on one face only.

family_scale1__Z_00430_2.desc: A compact alignment punch formed as a stepped round shank integral to a short polygonal grip collar, with the working end finished as a flat-faced conical center point. The shank has one milled longitudinal flat and a shallow annular groove for a sealing ring, while the collar is drilled with two small radial cross holes.

family_scale1__Z_00770_1.part_family: tapered flat sheet-metal spring strip (wedge clip)
family_scale1__Z_00770_1.desc: A flat wedge tongue tapered over its whole length but forked at the wide end into two parallel prongs separated by a central slot. A single round cross-hole passes through the wide head for a pivot pin, and one transverse stamped rib across the mid-span stiffens the bending section; thickness changes by a clean step rather than a curl, with all prong tips chamfered.

family_scale1__Z_00523_0.desc: One constant-thickness sheet, laser-cut as a ladder of small rectangular leaflets tied by narrow stems; transverse kerf slots set the leaflet pitch and the strip is folded so the stems form a gently curved central rachis that forks into a few side branches, with leaflets bent alternately to opposite sides and slightly twisted for volume. No holes, bosses or ribs; every junction is a small-radius bend fillet, giving an open thin-wall shell rather than a solid.

family_scale1__Z_00768_0.desc: Thin uniform flat plate formed as a round washer-like disc with a single concentric through bore for a shaft, plus an integral narrow pointer tab projecting radially from one side of the rim and tapering to a sharp across-flat apex; constant sheet thickness throughout with plain edges and no bends, ribs, or bosses.

family_scale1__Z_00108_2.desc: A low-profile rectangular bezel frame that is fully open through the middle with no floor, having a continuous gasket groove molded around the top rim. One short wall is cut with several elongated connector slots and the long walls are braced by sparse diagonal ribs; four external mounting ears with counterbored holes project from the corners and all outer edges are chamfered rather than rounded.

family_scale1__Z_00331_2.part_family: thin open-center rectangular plastic bezel frame
family_scale1__Z_00331_2.desc: Square thin sealing frame with a partial closed membrane spanning the window and an overmolded elastomer sealing bead on one face. Opposite sides have unequal rim widths to clear a hinge, six corner and edge fillets are used, a row of small vent slots runs along one inner wall, and four countersunk screw bosses stand proud of the back face at the corners.

family_scale1__Z_00457_1.part_family: molded thin-wall keypad faceplate with display window
family_scale1__Z_00457_1.desc: A low-profile front panel for a desktop calculator: a flat molded plate with a wide rectangular display cutout near the top and a larger grid of round key holes arranged in five columns by four rows below, plus one oblong side slot for a sliding selector. Instead of a raised rim it has a shallow recessed key field, a continuous snap groove around the back edge, and several internal cylindrical bosses with pilot holes for board mounting screws.

family_scale1__Z_00160_0.desc: A single narrow constant-thickness metal ribbon forms the whole part; the long middle span is die-set as a shallow offset band that runs parallel to, but raised from, two flat end tabs, with short bent transition zones at each end. In plan one long edge stays straight while the opposite edge steps inward at both ends, and every transition uses tight bend radii; there are no holes, bosses, or ribs.

family_scale1__Z_00736_0.part_family: bent flat-strip metal bracket / leaf strap
family_scale1__Z_00736_0.desc: A slender flat bar of constant rectangular cross-section, formed as one continuous piece with a single shallow knee bend that splits it into a long straight leg and a short end tab. The tab is pierced by one round through-hole near a square-to-slightly-oblique cut tip, the bend has a small inside fillet, and the edges are plain sheared with no ribs, slots, bosses, or secondary holes.

family_scale1__Z_00666_1.desc: A shorter straight carrier strip of the same thin laddered construction, but with three large rounded-rectangular lightening windows and a single centerline row of equal through holes. Both ends terminate in simple one-hole tabs, with a raised edge bead and no forked connector.

family_scale1__Z_00659_1.part_family: extruded personalized word fob (script name plate)
family_scale1__Z_00659_1.desc: A two-line stacked version: a short raised word over a longer signature, both carried on a thin closed oval rim that is extruded to the same depth; the rim acts as the joining shell, the strokes are kept as spaced islands tied to the rim by short ligatures, and a small round through-hole is pierced at each end of the oval for a cord.

family_scale1__Z_00544_0.desc: One-piece flat rectangular ring panel of uniform thin stock with a large central rectangular through-opening. The four border legs are joined into a closed frame and carry a repeated grid of small blind rectangular pockets, mixing square cells and elongated slots, separated by narrow ribs; the outer edge has a low continuous lip with small corner and edge reliefs.

family_scale1__Z_00632_1.desc: Short single-sided heatsink extrusion built from a thick flat base with a comb of tall parallel plates on one face. The opposite face is flat for mounting, with a pair of countersunk holes and one central longitudinal T-slot; fin roots are generously filleted and the fin tips are rounded.

family_scale1__Z_00558_2.desc: Hexagonal multi-slot profile segment with T-slots on alternating faces and closed lands between them. It has one large central clear bore surrounded by several equally spaced axial pin holes, plus tapped cross-holes that break through the closed faces; external corners use generous chamfers instead of round radii.

family_scale1__Z_00812_2.desc: A wider stamped plate whose edges are folded into a shallow channel for stiffness, the web opened by a central diamond-and-triangle truss pattern. One end is curled into a hinge barrel with a through bore while the other splits into two spring tabs, each slotted with an obround adjustment hole, and the raw edges are hemmed rather than laminated.

family_scale1__Z_00417_2.part_family: thin flat faceplate with an in-line row of raised rectangular bosses
family_scale1__Z_00417_2.desc: A longer narrow strip of the same family is formed with a right-angle mounting flange along one long edge and carries four equal rectangular bosses in two staggered rows on the web. The bosses have small base fillets, and a slotted clearance hole is placed near one end for adjustment.

family_scale1__Z_00599_1.desc: A similar sprocket-wheel variant could be a solid web disc with the same toothed outer rim, six shallow radial stiffening ribs on one face instead of open windows, and a plain central bore with a single keyway; the hub is flush and all teeth share one constant face width.

family_scale1__Z_00385_1.desc: A straight double-ended rocker of the same boss-and-blade family: one central through-bored hub carries two identical flat blades projecting from opposite sides in the same plane. Each blade joins the hub at mid-height with concave fillets on both edges and finishes in a small cross-drilled pin ear instead of a square tip, while the hub bore is counterbored from both faces and cut with a single internal keyway; there are no ribs or slots.

family_scale1__Z_00241_0.part_family: flat multi-arm hand knob / spider plate
family_scale1__Z_00241_0.desc: Thin constant-thickness plate with a round central hub and through bore; three identical arms radiate equally from the hub and blend with generous fillets into rounded end pads, each pad carrying a hexagonal recessed pocket, with all outside edges uniformly rounded.

family_scale1__Z_00640_1.part_family: cut-to-length T-slot sigma aluminum structural framing extrusion
family_scale1__Z_00640_1.desc: Light single-cell framing extrusion: one square hollow tube with constant thin wall and no draft, a small central bore, and one T-slot centered on each of the four outside faces. Add four internal corner gussets, fully rounded external corners, a longer square-cut body, two cross-drilled fixing holes near one end, and a shallow locating counterbore on the same end.

family_scale1__Z_00660_2.desc: Make a feed-through splice version with several cavity modules clipped to a shared open-back carrier and blank spacer bays between populated bays. Use end-only latches, a continuous central web, removable thin dividers, small round tooling holes, and larger corner fillets instead of paired side latch towers.

family_scale1__Z_00273_0.part_family: stamped and bent strip-metal hook / flat spring latch
family_scale1__Z_00273_0.desc: A single long slender flat strip of uniform thin rectangular section, monolithic and shaped only by stamping and bending. One end is curled into an open hook built from compound fillet bends with a short band of fine repeated ribs just behind it and a tiny rectangular lug at the crown; the straight shank carries one through-hole reinforced by a raised swaged collar on the face with a small edge tab at the same station, and the far end has both corners chamfered into a blunt lead-in point.

family_scale1__Z_00385_0.desc: A one-piece solid lug-and-blade lever: at one end a short cylindrical ring boss (a tube wall around a single centered through pin bore) stands with its axis through the lug, and a thin flat rectangular blade leaves the boss radially at about the boss mid-height. The blade is much thinner than the boss is tall, blends into the boss through an S-curved neck that is tangent on top and a concave fillet undercut beneath, then runs straight to a plain square-cut tip. The bore is a plain through hole with no counterbore, thread, keyway, rib, slot, or secondary hole; the only transitions are the boss-to-blade fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00447_0.part_family: shallow rectangular sheet cover panel with edge flange
family_scale1__Z_00447_0.desc: Flat near-square thin panel formed as two sheet layers joined on a straight seam, giving a stepped split visible in plan and a mid-height joint on the edge. One long edge carries a narrow raised lip/flange; faces carry slight draft so corners sit a touch off square, with one hidden bend/seam line on the face, no holes, bosses, ribs or noticeable fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00022_1.part_family: flat perforated multi-arm spider mounting plate
family_scale1__Z_00022_1.desc: A four-lobed plate of the same family with arms in a cross layout around a central through bore. Each rounded lobe tip holds a counterbored mounting hole, two bolt circles of small through-holes cross the arms, and short radial ribs stand on one face of the web between the bore and the lobe roots.

family_scale1__Z_00724_1.desc: A similar carrier ring uses a solid flanged outer band and a larger central collar connected by six straight radial ribs. Eight countersunk mounting holes alternate with lightening slots, and one rib carries a small locating boss for orientation.

family_scale1__Z_00389_2.desc: A split annular shim in the same family, opened by one radial slot running from the bore to the rim, with four evenly spaced through-holes across the face and a narrow raised boss encircling the bore on one side only; the outer edge uses plain chamfers instead of a face recess.

family_scale1__Z_00188_1.desc: Flanged servo timing sprocket with two integral retaining flanges and a single peripheral tooth band. A slightly dished web uses six oval lightening slots, and the split clamp hub has a plain bore, radial clamp slot, and transverse screw boss.

family_scale1__Z_00380_2.part_family: slender contact pin / socket terminal on a small rectangular base block
family_scale1__Z_00380_2.desc: A short machined pin pressed into a molded square header boss. The pin has a pointed mating end, a smooth solder tail and a barbed retention section with an undercut shoulder at the boss; the boss adds two mounting holes and one polarizing rib on a side face.

family_scale1__Z_00477_1.desc: A circular wreath-style flat badge with an off-center star: radial spokes connect an outer ring to an inner medallion, short tie webs stiffen the spoke roots, and two keyhole slots in the ring provide hanging features.

family_scale1__Z_00720_0.desc: Small square-section metal extrusion cut to a short fixed length with plain square ends; each of the four faces carries one continuous longitudinal T-slot, surrounding a central through bore, with hollow corner webs, small internal corner radii and consistently rounded outer edges.

family_scale1__Z_00772_0.part_family: thin flat rectangular panel with softly rounded edges
family_scale1__Z_00772_0.desc: A single monolithic thin slab whose footprint is a rectangle with four equally rounded corners and whose narrow side wall is fully bull-nosed, so the top and bottom perimeter edges carry the same small radius and meet at mid-thickness, giving eight rounded corner edges in all. The top and bottom faces are flat, parallel and featureless: no holes, slots, pockets, ribs or bosses, just a plain soft-edged cover plate.

family_scale1__Z_00719_0.part_family: thin toothed wheel on a spindle
family_scale1__Z_00719_0.desc: A flat circular gear-like web carries one continuous row of small external teeth around its rim, with repeating radial gullets. A slender round spindle is fixed coaxially through the centre, square to the web, extending as a long shaft on one side and a short stub on the other; the body has no spokes, hub boss, keyway, or rim slots.

family_scale1__Z_00680_0.desc: A straight, constant-cross-section extruded strip of compact rectangular outline, made as one solid finned body rather than assembled panels. All outer faces carry dense longitudinal micro-fins whose crests and roots are fully rounded, with the tooth count and pitch changing from face to face, and three small axial through-bores run end to end through the central web with no transverse features.

family_scale1__Z_00367_0.desc: A flat, uniform-thickness stamped blank with a stadium outline: long gently cambered top and bottom edges closing into small full-round ends. Two parallel rows of small through-holes track the long edges with a few extra holes across the width; near one rounded tip sits a short shaped pierce with adjacent pin holes for a buckle or fastener, while the opposite tip is left plain, and every corner is filleted with no formed ribs.

family_scale1__Z_00062_0.desc: A thin constant-thickness plate with a three-lobe clover outline that wraps four equal through bores: one central bore and three bores spaced evenly around it. Circular rims around each bore are joined by narrow webs pierced with small triangular relief windows, the outer edge dips into concave saddles between lobes, and all edges carry small rounds with tiny notches at the lobe crowns.

family_scale1__Z_00154_1.part_family: spinner-style multi-arm plate with hex nut-capture bosses
family_scale1__Z_00154_1.desc: A cross-shaped four-arm variant of the same plate family: a square central hub with a large through-bore joins four tapered arms at right angles, each arm tip carrying a low hexagonal nut-capture socket. The hub bore is counterbored from the top face, shallow stiffening ribs run along the underside of each arm, and the outline is chamfered all around.

family_scale1__Z_00115_2.part_family: slatted chair frame of thin rectangular panels
family_scale1__Z_00115_2.desc: Backless stool/side-table member of the same family: four legs framed by aprons into a square open top, with a single recessed lower shelf and vertical slats only on two opposite apron faces. The shelf panel carries one slim central slot and rounded top edges, joints are pinned stub-tenons rather than through-tenons, and the whole piece keeps the thin rectangular panel construction with uniform edge-break fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00669_1.desc: A rectangular drop-in divider frame of the same family, arranged as a six-by-three lattice of open cells with no solid floor, so the crisscross ribs and perimeter wall alone form the part. Two opposite outer walls carry scalloped finger notches for lifting, each interior rib crossing has a small drain slot at its lower edge, and the perimeter wall stands taller than the internal ribs with a short locating lip around its underside.

family_scale1__Z_00769_1.desc: A fully closed rounded-rectangle bezel of the same rolled-edge flat strip, with the two strip ends met and joined by a small welded butt seam hidden on one straight side. Two punched mounting holes sit on the base leg and a shallow registration notch is formed on the opposite side, while the cross-section remains a thin plain band.

family_scale1__Z_00600_1.desc: A flat, symmetrical through-truss bridge frame with two identical vertical side trusses joined by top lateral struts and sway bracing and by portal frames at both ends. The web uses a Pratt pattern of vertical posts and diagonals over an even number of equal bays, the bottom chords double as deck stringers, and each truss sits on square bearing plates with anchor-hole patterns plus small gusset plates at every node.

family_pilot__Z_00038_1.desc: A bent sheet-metal mounting bracket with a rectangular base flange and one upright flange folded at a right angle along a single bend. The upright carries two slotted mounting holes and one round clearance hole, with a small triangular gusset folded between the flanges and a hemmed outer edge for stiffness.

family_scale1__Z_00256_0.desc: Shallow rectangular end plate with large corner rounds and a recessed circular dish on the front, pierced by one central large bulkhead port and three equal circular ports clustered around it. Each round port is ringed by its own small-hole bolt circle, the centre position adds counterbored fixings on a wider bolt circle, a slotted louvered vent band runs along one edge, and extra small through-holes pierce the thin side walls with many small edge fillets.

family_pilot__Z_00100_2.desc: A left-right symmetric variant that is wider than tall, built around a large central bore with a ring of small through-holes on a circular bolt pattern. Four corner ears carry slotted holes for adjustable mounting, a short ribbed skirt reinforces the perimeter, and lightening pockets sit between the ribs; the outline has large corner fillets plus two small alignment notches on the side edges.

family_scale1__Z_00396_2.desc: Lighter stamped variant with a plain edge: four small press-fit dowels in a square pattern on one face and one larger central boss on the opposite face. The boss carries a transverse cross-hole for a retaining pin, and three lightening holes are pierced through the web on a bolt circle.

family_pilot__Z_00034_1.desc: Three-lobe flat link plate in a triangular layout, with round pads joined by concave waist sections; one pad uses a slotted mounting hole, the center has a plain clearance hole, and the outline is fully filleted for laser-cut or stamped production.

family_scale1__Z_00488_2.desc: A sieve-plate variant that keeps the all-hole concept but changes the layout: the through-holes are grouped into several rectangular banks separated by solid web strips, with countersunk entrances on the top face and a denser cluster near the centre. The border has corner clearance holes, small pressed stand-off dimples on the back face, and one pair of keyhole hanging slots.

family_pilot__Z_00009_1.desc: Flat annular distribution plate with a wide clamping flange carrying a few counterbored mounting holes and a sealing O-ring groove, plus one large central inlet bore feeding radial spoke passages that open into staggered hole rows. The face uses a single hole size grouped in wedge sectors separated by solid webs, and the back has small integral standoff bosses.

family_scale1__Z_00314_0.desc: Flat rectangular pressed-metal grille whose face carries a single vertical column of thirteen horizontal louvered slots inside a shallow raised border. A small rectangular hood projects from the upper area; two opposed side ears end in round eyelets and countersunk through-holes for screw fastening, while the perimeter is hemmed into a shallow channel and the many corners are broken with small chamfers.

family_scale1__Z_00571_0.desc: One solid rectangular prismatic block whose top face carries a single two-by-four grid of short cylindrical studs formed in the same piece. Matching vertical bores run through the core on the same grid, with some through and some blind, so a cross-section shows a hatched web between holes; the outer side walls and base are plain and flat with only small edge breaks.

family_scale1__Z_00040_1.desc: Asymmetric constant-thickness bracket plate with one long edge rail, a short return rail, three triangular lightening openings, and a single offset mounting foot. Round through holes are mixed with one keyhole slot, using large exterior radii and small internal fillets.

family_pilot__Z_00036_2.desc: A longer guide variant uses an open C-section with one mid-span latch and two fixed end hooks; the floor has elongated slots and a single alignment aperture near one hook. Interior stiffening ribs run in long-and-short bays, and the mounting feet are gusseted rather than plain tabs.

family_scale1__Z_00732_2.desc: A low-profile two-piece connector shell frame with an offset D-shaped cable exit on its rear wall and a mixed attachment scheme of threaded metal inserts on one edge and spring-clip latch openings on the other. Ventilation slots pierce the side walls, a single polarization rib projects into the window, external markings are omitted, and material is locally thickened around just the corner mounting holes.

family_scale1__Z_00187_0.part_family: flat radial multi-spoke spider hub plate
family_scale1__Z_00187_0.desc: This part is a single uniform-thickness plate: a central round hub with a through mounting bore and a cross-key feature carries six flat rectangular radial arms arranged as three diametrically opposite pairs, giving a six-point star outline with no continuous rim. Each spoke blends into the hub with small root fillets and has chamfered long edges and a square tip, using two chamfer classes (larger on the main opposite arms, smaller on the diagonal arms); there are no tall walls, ribs, or pockets beyond the flat web and raised hub face.

family_scale1__Z_00528_1.part_family: flat serpentine flexure plate (labyrinth-slotted thin panel)
family_scale1__Z_00528_1.desc: Circular flexure diaphragm with a solid outer annulus linked to a central round boss by four identical Archimedean spiral arms cut as through slots at even angular spacing. Ligament width is constant, each arm root blends into the rim and boss with a generous fillet, and a small relief hole sits at each spiral origin; the face is otherwise plain.

family_pilot__Z_00097_1.part_family: long thin flat strip / spacer bar
family_pilot__Z_00097_1.desc: A slender flat strap of uniform width and thickness with a row of evenly spaced circular through-holes along its centerline. Both ends are finished as semicircular rounds rather than tabs, and the faces remain flat and featureless between the holes. The part is one solid body with no bends, flanges, or bosses.

family_scale1__Z_00445_0.desc: One-piece thin plate of constant wall thickness built from a large central annular hub and three smaller identical annular rings set symmetrically around it. Each satellite ring is tied to the central hub by a short waisted tangential web, leaving open triangular windows, and every bore passes straight through the plate. One hub carries an across-flats seating feature, the web roots are filleted, small radial relief notches sit at the ring-to-web junctions, and neither face has protruding ribs or bosses.

family_scale1__Z_00386_0.part_family: roll-formed thin sheet-metal arch cover (open shroud)
family_scale1__Z_00386_0.desc: Constant-thickness sheet-metal shell roll-formed into an open-bottom segmental arch that is prismatic along its length; the crown is flattened into a short flat ridge running end to end with two smooth tangent radii down to each side fall, giving two longitudinal tangent edges in plan and a thin annular arch face at each open end. A single transverse half-round saddle is cut through the shell, rising from the lower edge on the near side and continuing as a hidden arc over the crown, with plain sheared edges and no holes, ribs or bosses.

family_scale1__Z_00651_1.desc: A longer rail of the same rectangular section whose top face is a continuous comb of identical narrow blind slots at a steady pitch from end to end. One wider window near the middle breaks fully through the thickness, both ends carry counterbored mounting holes, and each side wall has a shallow full-length relief groove with a small external chamfer.

family_scale1__Z_00706_0.desc: Flat rectangular thin-wall panel with a smooth show face and an integral low perimeter rim on the back. A single row of tall, evenly spaced vertical ribs ties into the rim and divides the interior into a series of deep narrow rectangular pockets of uniform depth, with one end pocket made narrower; the thin webs leave a continuous front skin and the rim corners are essentially square with small edge fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00237_1.part_family: T-slot structural aluminum extrusion cut length
family_scale1__Z_00237_1.desc: Rectangular aluminum framing extrusion segment that is wider than it is deep, cut square at both ends. The two broad faces each hold two parallel longitudinal T-grooves while the narrow edge faces are closed and smooth, and straight longitudinal webs split the interior into several chambers around two side-by-side fastener bores. Outer corners are chamfered rather than rounded, and one end is cross-drilled through both walls for a locking pin.

family_scale1__Z_00546_1.desc: A broader flat spacer bar of the same drilled-rail family: a single thick rectangular strip with one central row of larger through-holes alternating with elongated slots, plus two blind counterbored mounting holes near each end. One long edge is milled with a shallow keyway, the opposite edge and end breaks are chamfered, the corners are left square, and there are no internal bores.

family_scale1__Z_00679_2.desc: A stamped sheet-metal eight-arm spider with alternating long and short arms around a shallow dished hub; every arm tip is bent up into a small lug pierced by an elongated slot, and narrow radial lightening slots run along each arm rather than round holes. A ring of small pilot holes surrounds the dished center, and short embossed spokes stiffen the hub-to-arm transition; the outer edge is left plain with no eyelets or hex seats.

family_scale1__Z_00506_1.desc: Compact four-position terminal bar formed as a shallow insulating trough carrying a straight conductive blade. Round wire holes and square captive-nut pockets alternate along the blade, stamped divider ribs separate poles, one end is stopped and the other open, with two snap feet under the carrier.

family_scale1__Z_00400_1.desc: A bowed flat-strap link with an identical thickness throughout, carrying a closed cylindrical eye at each end so the piece acts as a short connector rather than a hook. One eye has a plain through pin-hole while the other is preceded by a single elongated slot in the arm, and the otherwise plain strap has two small coined locating dimples near the midspan.

family_scale1__Z_00003_2.part_family: thin flat multi-window carrier frame / bezel strip with edge latch notches
family_scale1__Z_00003_2.desc: A narrow single-row stamped carrier strip with four elongated capsule-shaped slots for sliding contacts, formed as a flat skeleton with no recessed floor. One long edge is turned up into a continuous hinge flange with curled tangs, the opposite edge carries sprung finger-latch tabs, the webs between slots are pierced with small round tooling holes, and the two ends terminate in forked locating prongs with softly blended fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00816_0.part_family: slender thin-wall tubular probe / needle shaft
family_scale1__Z_00816_0.desc: One straight, constant-round thin-wall tube with a full-length axial bore forms the whole part; the smooth cylindrical shell has no threads, ribs, bosses, slots or flanges. A single small diametral cross-hole sits close to one end, and both ends are essentially plain open cuts with only light edge breaks.

family_scale1__Z_00056_2.desc: Closed-cup variant with the ribbing inverted: a deep one-ended annular shell carries external axial splines, a single side port is rotated to run parallel to the axis, the rim holds an integral snap-latch cantilever, the mating face has a continuous seal groove, and the closed back is stiffened by a waffle grid of ribs instead of a pocket.

family_scale1__Z_00598_1.part_family: toothed/serrated flanged ring on a cylindrical hub with through bore
family_scale1__Z_00598_1.desc: A flat annular serrated washer of the same family but without an extended hub: a thin ring gripped between mating faces, serrated on both faces near the outer edge, with a round central bore interrupted by one axial keyway and a small counterbore from the back face. Several evenly spaced through holes sit on an inner pitch circle for weight reduction or pinning.

family_scale1__Z_00561_0.desc: A single constant-thickness flat plate cut to an irregular outer profile. A narrow neck at one end bridges into a circular annular eye lug pierced by one centered through hole; the wider body carries one large stepped open window with a rounded internal cut-in, one small isolated rectangular through-slot near the middle, several perimeter notches and stepped tabs, and filleted internal corners. All features are through-cuts in the sheet with no raised ribs or bosses.

family_scale1__Z_00256_2.desc: Round bulkhead version with a perimeter mounting flange and four equal circular connector ports spaced evenly on a ring around a central threaded cable-gland hole. The back face is stiffened by radial ribs between the port bosses, every port has three small threaded inserts rather than four, and there is no vent band, only a continuous seal groove inside the flange.

family_scale1__Z_00756_1.desc: Heavier flat drive plate with chain teeth around the full outside rim and an integral raised hub boss on one face. Instead of many drilled holes it uses a few large mounting slots, a keyed central bore, and several lightening pockets cut between short radial spokes, with generous fillets at the spoke roots.

family_scale1__Z_00772_1.part_family: thin flat rectangular panel with softly rounded edges
family_scale1__Z_00772_1.desc: A thin rounded-corner rectangular lid from the same panel family, but laid out as an enclosure cover: one face has a shallow recessed central field leaving a raised perimeter rim, each corner carries a small countersunk through-hole for fasteners, and two short blind vents sit along one long edge. The outer side wall keeps the same fully rounded soft edge and uniform small corner fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00032_2.desc: A flat T-shaped bracket plate with three plain clearance holes in the vertical ear and two horizontal adjustment slots in the base, joined by triangular relief cutouts at the web. It has constant plate thickness, filleted outside corners, and one long edge chamfered as an assembly lead-in, with no recessed pockets.

family_scale1__Z_00340_1.desc: A longer, symmetric annular-segment shell curved to a steady radius, with both straight edges turned up as short stiffening flanges. A circular through-hole sits near the inner radius, a row of evenly spaced small mounting holes follows the outer arc, and all internal corners are filleted while the faces remain otherwise flat.

family_scale1__Z_00421_0.part_family: thin flat multi-eyelet plate (spinner-style bossed flange)
family_scale1__Z_00421_0.desc: Single uniform-gauge flat plate whose plan outline is four annular bosses: one central eyelet and three matching satellite eyelets spaced equally on one bolt circle, all tied together by short tangent webs into a three-lobed profile. Each boss has a concentric through hole with a shallow counterbore and clean rounded outer rim; the three satellite holes share the bolt circle while the fourth sits on the center axis, and the part stays perfectly planar with pierced features only—no ribs, bends, or pockets.

family_scale1__Z_00354_1.desc: A molded curved channel rail uses an open trough section: a thin concave web with two side walls, intermittent transverse ribs underneath, and a smooth convex running face. One end is a slotted mounting ear and the other end has two coaxial pin bosses, with a few locating holes along the web and rounded free edges.

family_scale1__Z_00612_0.desc: A thin circular toothed rim carries eight evenly spaced rounded external teeth with filleted roots, and a concentric cylindrical hub projects axially from one face well beyond the rim thickness. A small through bore runs along the axis, opened by a larger coaxial counterbore at the hub end, and the hub blends into the web with a smooth shoulder fillet.

family_scale1__Z_00820_0.desc: A thin, flat circular plate formed as one continuous annulus between a central round through bore and a plain cylindrical outer rim. The annular web carries a single evenly spaced ring of identical arc-shaped through slots that sweep tangentially around the bore in a one-direction swirl; each slot is an obround capsule bent along a common radius with rounded ends, leaving curved spoke-like ligaments between the bore, the slot row and the rim. The disc is constant sheet thickness with no raised hub, ribs or bosses, only small edge breaks on the faces and slot edges.

family_scale1__Z_00254_2.part_family: flat multi-cell hub plate with central bore and polygonal through-cells
family_scale1__Z_00254_2.desc: A linear-strip member of the same family: a flat uniform-thickness bar links five through-openings in one row, a central round bore with two hexagonal cells stepped to each side, joined by narrow ligaments and widened into a mounting flange at one end with two slotted holes. Shallow blind pockets recess the back face between cells, the cell entrances are countersunk on the front, and the long outer edges are left square rather than rounded.

family_scale1__Z_00335_0.desc: A uniform thin metal strip formed as a long low spine with short end flanges, small downward legs, lanced tabs, notches and repeated narrow fingers along its length. A round mounting hole near one end and additional small pierced holes or slots break the strip; transitions are filleted and all features share one sheet thickness.

family_scale1__Z_00693_0.desc: One-piece plastic ring frame: a thin flat rounded-rectangle top flange with four corner through holes surrounds a central window, the inner lip is a continuous band of semicircular scallops, and matching short open half-barrel ribs hang from the flange around the loop, tied by thin webs to cradle round cells; outer corners are filleted and the pockets open through the top.

family_scale1__Z_00465_2.part_family: perforated slotted miniature metal rail strip
family_scale1__Z_00465_2.desc: A short formed bracket bent from the same slotted perforated profile into a shallow Z so the web is offset from the mounting flange. Holes populate only the outer flange, the slots are broken into short dash segments, and a few larger pierced windows with embossed locating dimples sit between hole groups.

family_scale1__Z_00167_0.desc: One-piece thin-walled rectangular hood whose closed front face is filled with a dense bank of long horizontal louvers set between vertical side ribs and a rounded-corner perimeter. A raised rectangular boss and small latch tab sit on the top edge, the rear steps into a narrower open cable neck, and the interior carries transverse stiffening webs plus a single small drilled boss hole.

family_scale1__Z_00065_1.desc: Two parallel thin rails are tied by evenly spaced transverse rungs into a ladder-like truss, forking into open clevis eyes at each end with one large pivot bore per side. Instead of diagonal bracing it uses rectangular lightening pockets along the rails, an elongated adjustment slot mid-span, and a single central boss row.

family_pilot__Z_00047_0.desc: A flat rectangular backplate with a shallow folded edge has three narrow horizontal rails carried across one face in a regular vertical rhythm. The rails read as full-width raised bands joined to the plate with small end returns and filleted or hemmed edges, leaving open gaps between bands; the visible feature set is plate-and-rail only, with no prominent through-holes, slots, or bosses.

family_scale1__Z_00087_0.desc: A flat, constant-thickness three-lobed spider plate: a central web with one large through bore branches through concave, filleted arms into three raised boss clusters, all sharing one scalloped outline. The face carries a ring of six plain through holes plus three double-D two-flat anti-rotation holes at the ears, with small recessed pockets between bosses, and the edge profile is a plain rectangular band with cored internal detail.

family_scale1__Z_00055_0.desc: A thin upright carrier plate with a continuous perimeter flange and a regular two-by-four array of open rectangular box cells formed to one face; the cells share a common back web, have drafted walls and filleted mouths, and are separated by narrow intersecting ribs. One edge forms a low foot with two short upstanding locator rails, and small raised keying bosses sit at the cell openings.

family_scale1__Z_00428_0.desc: Thin flat metal stamping of uniform sheet thickness: a small round lug pierced with a single through-hole at the narrow tip, a short bent retaining nib folded beside the lug, and a tapering neck that flares into one large fully radiused teardrop paddle end; the outline is one closed symmetric blank with generous fillets at the neck blend.

family_scale1__Z_00269_2.desc: Closed castellated adjustment ring with an internal spline and numerous external locking teeth. Alternate teeth are relieved by lightweight pockets, four threaded inserts sit at quarter points, and a spring-latch tab bridges a narrow axial slot instead of using a clevis.

family_scale1__Z_00730_1.part_family: slender arched thin-strip catch hook (formed ribbon pawl)
family_scale1__Z_00730_1.desc: A straighter stamped flat-strip pawl of uniform thickness with just a slight bow: a round pivot hole and a short adjustment slot sit at the mounting end, a small coined circular boss reinforces the pivot zone, and the working end is bent up into a single hook tooth. Outer edges are broken, faces are plain, and there are no ribs.

family_scale1__Z_00699_2.desc: A wide multi-cell rail segment with an H-like web pattern, two rows of longitudinal clearance bores, and three internal webs. T-slots open only on the two broad faces while the narrow edges stay closed; one face has chamfered slot lips, the opposite face has radiused lips, and the cut ends carry counterbored fastener features.

family_scale1__Z_00329_1.part_family: small single-column pedestal stand with splayed foot base
family_scale1__Z_00329_1.desc: Taller member of the same pedestal family using a round top disk on a cylindrical center tube. Three equally spaced legs splay from a lower hub to curved foot pads, with a bolted top flange on the tube, teardrop gussets under the disk, and a continuous ring linking the legs partway down.

family_pilot__Z_00021_1.desc: A one-piece molded plastic program camshaft with two clusters of four-lobed cams separated by an integral spur gear at mid-length. One end is a plain bearing journal, the other a splined drive stub, and each cam lobe carries a molded radial rib with lightening holes between the hub and lobe tips.

family_scale1__Z_00343_2.part_family: thin slotted grille panel with mounting bosses
family_scale1__Z_00343_2.desc: A squarer lattice bezel with a dense field of equal square through-openings set in a thin outer frame. It uses integral corner posts for screws, adds snap-fit tabs along the side edges, and recesses the central area slightly, with all window corners chamfered and a fine rib network tying the frame together.

family_scale1__Z_00005_0.desc: A long injection-molded thermoplastic bridge: a thin central web connects two taller end blocks through sloped transition walls, all as one uniform shell. Each end block has a circular through-hole crowned by a knurled captive thumb wheel, while beneath each end a pair of downward resilient legs forms an inverted channel with chamfered snap tips; a wide rectangular window runs along the top between the holes, with small edge notches and rounded junctions.

family_scale1__Z_00384_1.desc: A straight folded sheet-metal channel trim whose flat base web carries two short flanges bent to the same side, with a small safety hem rolled along one free edge. A regular row of round mounting holes is pierced through the web, and the ends are cropped square.

family_scale1__Z_00729_2.desc: A compact S-shaped flat-spring clip formed from similar thin strip stock, with a short central web and two opposed cantilever arms folded back in opposite directions. One arm carries a single pierced mounting hole beside a small coined boss, the other arm ends in a chamfered lead-in tongue, and two raised dimple detents plus a locally doubled-over edge provide seating and stiffness.

family_scale1__Z_00452_2.desc: A round vent style grille of the same family: a ring-shaped outer frame with a short cylindrical skirt is infilled by radial spokes crossing three concentric rings rather than an irregular mesh. Two opposed integral spring clips on the skirt provide push-fit retention, a small recessed logo pad interrupts one ring, and the rim uses a rolled edge with generous fillets instead of sharp chamfers.

family_scale1__Z_00218_0.desc: A thin constant-thickness flat blade with a short, thicker rectangular mounting head at one end and a fully rounded tip at the other. The head has one through mounting hole and a couple of tiny end slots, steps down through a small shoulder into the blade, and the blade carries a dense repeating pattern of small rectangular through-windows plus a long row of fine edge chamfers, with a few grouped short and paired slots near the head; the tip corners are radiused.

family_scale1__Z_00226_2.part_family: rectangular open-grid frame with connector bosses
family_scale1__Z_00226_2.desc: Wider variant laid out with three rows of square openings plus an extra central spine, its rear face ribbed into shallow pockets between the mullion junctions for stiffness. Diagonal corners hold metal inserts for jackscrews and the other corners are plain locating pins, with molded latch hooks on the short sides in place of connector housings.

family_scale1__Z_00700_2.part_family: thin flat polygonal aperture retainer plate
family_scale1__Z_00700_2.desc: A thin flat rounded-triangular shutter plate with one central oblong slotted opening rather than a round hole. Two parallel raised stiffening ribs run across one face beside the slot, small cylindrical bosses with through holes sit at the three corners for fasteners, and a continuous shallow groove near the perimeter serves as a seal seat.

family_pilot__Z_00041_1.desc: A uniform-thickness right-triangular gusset plate bounded by two perpendicular legs and a diagonal outer edge. The inner corner is relieved by a concave quarter-round cutout, three clearance holes are patterned along the two legs, and the outer vertices are rounded rather than pointed.

family_scale1__Z_00523_1.desc: Flat-pack tabletop tree from a single equal-thickness plate: a straight trunk splits into symmetric opposed branches, each branch carrying two ranked rows of rectangular leaves separated by repeat kerf slots; all leaves are folded to alternating angles while the lower trunk is bent into a short L foot for standing. No fasteners or bosses, corners broken only by bend radii.

family_scale1__Z_00417_0.part_family: thin flat faceplate with an in-line row of raised rectangular bosses
family_scale1__Z_00417_0.desc: A constant-thickness rectangular plate with one flat rear face and, on the front face, a single row of three small solid rectangular pads standing a short uniform height above the panel. The pads are separated by clear gaps, clustered toward one side of the plate, and have square edges with no through-holes, slots, ribs, or noticeable fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00165_1.desc: Flat, unbent rectangular splice plate from the same toothed-sheet family: a single elongated central window leaves two solid side rails, and stamped teeth cover only the two long edges for pressing into adjacent timber members. Corners are square, there are no diagonal ribs, and the plate is meant to lie in one plane as a butt-joint mending plate.

family_scale1__Z_00160_1.desc: A shorter, wider spring contact: a flat mounting pad carries two round through-holes and a lanced retention barb, while a narrow cantilever finger leaves the pad through one tight bend and ends in a raised stamped contact dimple. A folded return near the root presets the preload, and all corners use small bend radii rather than sharp fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00790_2.desc: Double-helical drive sleeve with two opposed tooth bands separated by a central relief groove around a stout cylinder. It uses a splined through-bore instead of a hex hole, adds a circumferential oil groove and two set-screw flats, and keeps smooth pilot lands at both ends.

family_scale1__Z_00007_2.desc: A split six-point star spring ring: the band is cut through at one valley so it can expand over a shaft, each star tip is twisted slightly out of plane to act like a lock-washer tooth, and small notches are stamped at alternating inner corners to increase compliance.

family_scale1__Z_00498_0.part_family: square-cell honeycomb cartridge in cylindrical shell
family_scale1__Z_00498_0.desc: A thin-walled cylindrical sleeve is lined with a full-length square-cell honeycomb monolith whose orthogonal webs form open axial through-channels and are joined to the bore. Both ends are open and flush, the lattice sits inset within a plain round rim, and the web junctions have small node fillets with no external bosses or ports.

family_pilot__Z_00097_2.part_family: long thin flat strip / spacer bar
family_pilot__Z_00097_2.desc: A thin elongated strip formed with a narrow flange folded along one long edge, giving an L-shaped cross-section. Two oblong slots are punched through the flat leg near opposite ends, and a single shallow bend offsets one end of the strip. All other surfaces are flat, with small bend radii and no additional ribs or holes.

family_scale1__Z_00045_0.desc: Straight slender rail built from a thin-wall rectangular tube, with one broad face cut into four rectangular window bays having large corner radii so only narrow transverse ribs and a solid back wall remain; each bay carries a four-hole through pattern on a common bolt circle, the long edges are scalloped with many small semicircular notches, and the ends are closed with rounded caps.

family_scale1__Z_00660_1.desc: Make a single-ended board header from the same family: one low multi-row cavity block stands over a closed rear shroud, while the other end becomes a smooth cap with a polarization rib and two screw-ear bosses. Keep the latching asymmetric, with a barbed arm on one side and a plain guide rib on the other.

family_scale1__Z_00173_0.desc: Mirror-symmetric molded carrier whose low central bridge joins two outward-leaning upright towers. Each tower has a sloped face with a row of round connector bores plus small cross holes, hex across-flats seats and a ribbed collar at the top; the lower edge ends in two opposed radiused hook feet with through holes, and the whole body is a constant-thickness shell with side ribs and filleted internal corners.

family_scale1__Z_00263_2.desc: A wider asymmetric member of the family keeps the flat sheet-metal frame idea but mixes features: one long mounting leg is pierced with a linear run of many small holes and two obround adjustment slots, while a shorter return leg carries several raised press-fit bosses and coined locating dimples instead of some through-holes. Shallow lanced stiffening ribs run along the long leg beside the central rectangular aperture, and the free ends are finished with small rounded pads rather than a fine lance comb.

family_scale1__Z_00369_2.desc: An elongated two-end spinner link of thin uniform plate with a large bearing bore at each end and a smaller central finger bore. A wide gently waisted web connects the two end bosses, each end boss carries a raised retaining ring on one face only, and the outer contour is a smooth continuous radius blend without lobes or spokes.

family_scale1__Z_00398_2.part_family: round-bar spacer with axial bores and a longitudinal milled flat
family_scale1__Z_00398_2.desc: A short stout eccentric barrel, round except for a wide full-length keyseat milled into one side. A single off-center axial through-bore is crossed near mid-length by one transverse radial hole through the wall while the thick rim opposite the keyseat is left solid; both ends are faced square with a small external chamfer.

family_scale1__Z_00277_1.desc: External-tooth curved rack bent into a near half-ring, with the gear teeth on the outer convex edge and a thicker plain rim on the inner side. A row of evenly spaced through holes runs along the neutral line for bolting to a rotating hub, with a single radial keyway slot at mid-arc; both ends are square-cut and counterbored.

family_scale1__Z_00472_1.part_family: webbed radial spider hub with end eyes
family_scale1__Z_00472_1.desc: Three-arm version of the same family with arms at 120 degrees: a thicker splined central boss with a keyway carries three tapered lattice arms, each terminating in a clevis fork (paired ears sharing one cross pin hole) rather than a single eye; triangular lightening pockets pierce the webs, a raised pilot flange stands off one hub face, and there are no across-flats pads.

family_scale1__Z_00772_2.part_family: thin flat rectangular panel with softly rounded edges
family_scale1__Z_00772_2.desc: A thin soft-edged rectangular bezel rather than a solid blank: the body is a flat ring with a large centred rectangular through-opening, four corner mounting holes and a single row of small vent holes along one inner side. The exterior retains the fully rounded perimeter edge and matched corner radii, while the inner opening is left sharp with no recesses or bosses.

family_scale1__Z_00384_2.desc: A Z-profile sheet-metal stiffener strip with two parallel edge flanges offset by a central web, both free edges lightly hemmed for stiffness. It adds a pair of slotted mounting holes near mid-length and small relief notches at each end so it can sit over a mating lip.

family_scale1__Z_00178_1.desc: A double-hubbed spur gear has a thicker toothed rim with identical bosses protruding from both faces and a central splined bore instead of a plain hole. The web is pierced by several equally spaced lightening holes on a bolt circle, the boss roots are filleted, and the tooth tips are chamfered on both sides for easier meshing.

family_scale1__Z_00042_0.part_family: thin flat radial spider hub plate
family_scale1__Z_00042_0.desc: One continuous thin plate forms a central annular hub with a large plain through bore and a shallow concentric recess, with three short radial arms blending into faceted, roughly hexagonal outer pads. Each pad carries a pair of small blind holes (six total); the pad-to-arm transitions are generously filleted, the bore rim is slightly raised as a boss, and the outer edges are lightly chamfered.

family_scale1__Z_00321_0.desc: Thin circular annular plate carrying a dense peripheral ring of narrow radial fins on one face, with an open slot between adjacent fins. A raised cylindrical hub is blended into the plate center with a smooth fillet, holds a single square through-bore for a shaft, and shows concentric raised rings on its end face.

family_scale1__Z_00014_0.desc: One molded shell forms an elongated, gently rockered spine that climbs toward a tapered nose; from its lower midsection two banks of thin swept vanes splay downward and outward at matching oblique angles like paired multi-keel runners. The vanes are lengthwise ribbed, end in rounded tips, and sit in generous root fillets, while a central transverse boss carries a large stepped through-bore, a pair of small counterbored mounting holes and two upright pin bosses.

family_scale1__Z_00283_2.desc: Open rectangular sheet-metal spacer frame with two side rails and three cross straps for supporting a panel; one rail has clearance holes and the opposite rail has pressed threaded inserts, with flanged hems, corner fillets and a mirrored hole-and-slot pattern.

family_scale1__Z_00501_1.desc: Compact vertical-mount card-edge socket with a single continuous contact channel flanked by tall side walls, integrated latch towers at both ends with pivot bores, a closed bottom plate, two threaded metal inserts, and a staggered row of small alignment pegs instead of underside cutouts.

family_scale1__Z_00767_0.desc: A slender flat link formed by two thick circular end bosses joined through an open triangulated center web. Each boss carries one large through bore with small side lug features, while the web has an X-braced pocket, paired small through holes with shallow counterbores, lightening recesses, filleted internal corners, and a thin uniform wall.

family_scale1__Z_00621_0.part_family: vented extruded electronics enclosure with front I/O panel
family_scale1__Z_00621_0.desc: An elongated hollow rectangular shell, open at the rear and closed at the front by an integral I/O faceplate; the body is a thin-walled tube with internal longitudinal rails and a lower guide channel, plus a small side mounting tab with a hole near the front. The faceplate carries a four-by-four array of sixteen small rectangular ventilation slots above a stepped connector notch, one oblong rounded port opening and one square port opening, all within a recessed bezel with softly filleted outer edges.

family_scale1__Z_00295_2.desc: A panel-mount variant uses a deeper open box with flanged ears on two opposite sides and snap-fit grooves inside the remaining walls. It omits most through holes in favor of blind corner bosses, adds ventilation slots across the floor, a central oval grommet pass-through, and isolated rib islands around the component area.

family_scale1__Z_00748_0.desc: A welded triangular gusset bracket assembled from thin flat-bar strips and plate. Three outer bars are mitered and welded into an open acute triangular frame, and a thinner triangular web is set into the window and welded along its edges so the two stock thicknesses read as an outer rim with an inset rib; joints are sharp corner seams with small weld fillets rather than machined radii, and no through fasteners are used.

family_scale1__Z_00195_2.desc: A compact three-spoke variant used as a hand or drive wheel: a stout central boss with a D-shaped bore and an integral axial collar ties into a continuous outer rim whose outside is lightly textured for grip. Each spoke root has a triangular gusset fillet, a single index lug sits on the rim rather than four symmetric ears, and two of the three pockets between spokes carry small moulded balance pads.

family_scale1__Z_00342_1.part_family: bent sheet-metal angle bracket with machined mounting lugs
family_scale1__Z_00342_1.desc: Z-shaped formed sheet-metal bracket with two parallel flanges offset by a central web and sharing one inside bend radius throughout. One flange holds a single slotted mounting hole and a row of three small drilled holes while the opposite flange holds two large grommet holes; the web is stiffened by one pressed longitudinal bead, has two rectangular lightening windows, and the outer edges are hemmed for safety.

family_scale1__Z_00607_2.desc: An office floor model of the same family built as a repeating pattern: a central spine corridor flanked by six identical cubicle bays formed by short partition walls, with integrated desk and cabinet blocks rising from the base in each bay. A grid of small mounting holes covers the slab, and two larger rectangular wells mark service zones near the rear wall.

family_scale1__Z_00065_2.desc: A compact L-shaped member of the same ribbed thin-wall family: a short upright plate stiffened by closed triangular gussets and a continuous outer flange, standing on a flat foot. The foot has one keyhole mounting slot, the upright carries three raised threaded bosses, and the rear face is filled with a honeycomb field of small circular ribs rather than an open diagonal lattice.

family_scale1__Z_00684_2.part_family: lightweight lattice-ribbed twin-cheek bearing bracket (joint yoke)
family_scale1__Z_00684_2.desc: A boxed cast sibling: two taller cheek plates closed across the top by an integral cap, forming a rectangular crown over a single central pivot bore, with a clevis slot and cross-pin hole low down instead of an open saddle. Stiffening uses orthogonal I-beam webs between bosses rather than a lattice, mounting is from a pattern of four tapped bosses on the outer faces, and edges show draft with large casting fillets and no counterbored holes.

family_pilot__Z_00055_1.desc: An oblong, stadium-ended thin emblem plate with a raised rail following the perimeter and a recessed central legend band. A circular boss with a countersunk through hole sits near each rounded end for fastening, the front band is filled with a repeating chevron emboss, and the backside carries two locating pins plus short transverse stiffening ribs.

family_scale1__Z_00708_0.desc: A single thin rectangular cover plate with an integral shallow upturned perimeter rim and beveled corner facets. The flat central field carries a nine-by-ten pattern of small round through-holes inside a plain border, with small corner reliefs/fillets and no separate bosses.

family_pilot__Z_00094_2.desc: A forked contact blade split into two parallel tines at the working end, each tine carrying a small embossed contact bump, merging into a wider base tab with one slotted hole and a bent locating ear for retention.

family_scale1__Z_00518_0.part_family: thin-walled molded plastic bezel / instrument tray
family_scale1__Z_00518_0.desc: Injection-molded shallow rectangular panel with rounded corners and a stepped raised perimeter rim; the interior floor carries two side-by-side circular ring bosses, one rectangular sunken pocket, a small rounded-rectangle pad and several short standoff ribs, all blended by fillets over a thin, near-uniform wall.

family_scale1__Z_00540_2.desc: Four-bay ladder-frame variant: two side rails connect a perforated front bezel to a plain rear strap, with formed divider ribs separating four slotted bays and a mixed pattern of keyhole and round fixings.

family_scale1__Z_00203_2.desc: Solid hinge-leaf variant that drops the fork: one thick paddle carries a segmented barrel knuckle along a long edge with grease grooves between the knuckle lengths, and the opposite edge is an integral snap rail with two screw bosses and a short run of locating ribs. The slot is replaced by a keyhole opening and all corners use small equal radii.

family_scale1__Z_00721_2.part_family: bent sheet-metal ventilated channel / perforated folded enclosure rail
family_scale1__Z_00721_2.desc: A wide folded sheet-metal cover formed as a three-sided shallow tray with downturned side walls and a front mounting lip. The top is perforated by a dense rectangular grid of round vent holes, the side walls have stamped louvered vents, and the front lip is dotted with countersunk screw holes and a pair of obround cable slots.

family_scale1__Z_00669_0.desc: A shallow, roughly square injection-molded tray built from a flat base plate with an integral orthogonal lattice of thin vertical ribs, forming a four-by-four array of sixteen open-top square pockets. The outer perimeter is a low continuous wall of the same uniform thickness; the rib tops are flat and co-planar, the rib intersections are fully merged, and small fillets run along the rib-to-base junctions. There are no through holes, bosses, or fasteners, it is a single open grid shell with consistent wall thickness.

family_scale1__Z_00751_1.desc: A double-ended variant in the same thin sheet family: two similar annular eyes, each with its own through bore, are joined by a narrower straight web whose centerline passes through both bore centers, with one elongated lightening slot cut mid-span and smooth rounded blends where the web meets each ring.

family_pilot__Z_00114_1.desc: A heavier machined clamp collar made from thick rectangular-section ring stock, split once with two blocky lug pads facing across the gap; each pad holds a pair of through holes for two pinch bolts, with a small relief slot at the split, a light locating dowel between the pads, chamfered bore edges, and a shallow counterbore on the outer face.

family_pilot__Z_00079_0.desc: Constant-section prismatic profile: four equal radial wings meet at a compact central core, with narrow axial slots between wings and dense small longitudinal ribs on the outer faces. The core has a central through bore plus four evenly spaced through holes on a circular pattern; edges use many small rounds with a few larger fillets and chamfers.

family_scale1__Z_00537_2.desc: A heat-sink style extrusion with a dense field of longitudinal cooling fins standing off one broad face and a pair of dovetail guide grooves on the opposite face. A solid base web joins the two sides, contains one axial tie-rod bore offset from center, and the fin tips are rounded with staggered fin lengths across the width.

family_pilot__Z_00073_1.part_family: handled single-edged pointed blade (fixed utility knife)
family_pilot__Z_00073_1.desc: Symmetrical double-edged dagger blade with a central ridge and a milled fuller on each face running most of its length. Both edges are plain and continuously ground to a reinforced point, and a compact oval guard separates the blade from a waisted grip. A circular lanyard hole pierces the pommel, while the short ricasso and all body junctions are left unsharpened with small fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00069_1.desc: A thin metal grid plate with a denser square array of through holes across the face, four countersunk corner mounting bores, and two elongated slots along one side for adjustment. The outline is a clean rectangle with rounded corner fillets, a pair of small tooling holes near one edge, and light deburr chamfers on the hole rims rather than raised side tabs.

family_scale1__Z_00206_1.desc: A shorter, wider variant of the same C-yoke family with two ears of unequal length projecting from a stiffened back web rather than a tall patterned plate. The web carries a single central raised pad with a four-hole tapped pattern plus dowel holes and backside ribs; only the lower ear has a plain large cross bore, while the upper ear uses a slotted hole with a keyway. Ear tips are squared with small fillets at the roots and lightening slots cut through the web.

family_scale1__Z_00008_2.part_family: flat ribbed annular ring (fan/spacer) with radial vanes and mounting lugs
family_scale1__Z_00008_2.desc: A deeper, slightly dished version of the ribbed ring: a conical annular shell linking the bore hub to a flanged outer shroud, carrying twelve curved vanes rather than straight ribs. Six blind bosses around the rim accept threaded inserts, the central bore includes a keyway, and the back face has scalloped pockets for stiffness and weight reduction.

family_scale1__Z_00068_1.desc: A flat spoked drive pulley of the same moulded-wheel family: a keyed central boss connects through four broad tapered spokes to a thick grooved outer rim, with a full annular stiffening rib on the back face instead of a rib skirt. A few round lightening holes pierce the web between spokes, and the rim edge is plain rather than flanged.

family_scale1__Z_00582_0.part_family: flat profile-cut miniature rifle replica plate
family_scale1__Z_00582_0.desc: Uniform-thickness flat plate cut to the side silhouette of a carbine: a fixed buttstock with a triangular lightening opening, a separate downward pistol grip and magazine, and a long slim handguard/barrel. The handguard top edge carries many evenly spaced narrow cross-slots, its face is pierced by a dense regular row of small round through-holes, a tiny lanyard hole sits near the muzzle, and a low raised pad is formed on one flat face; all outside corners are broken with small fillets.

family_scale1__Z_00801_1.part_family: thin contoured flat metal latch/linkage plate
family_scale1__Z_00801_1.desc: Elongated flat lever plate from the same punched/milled sheet family: a straight arm linking a circular boss end with one primary pivot bore and a small secondary hole to a forked clevis end with a U-slot and two cross holes. The arm carries lightening cutouts, a short obround slot, and a formed stiffening bead, with every corner and opening rounded.

family_scale1__Z_00722_0.part_family: thin flat openwork lattice grille panel with bolt-circle mounting ears
family_scale1__Z_00722_0.desc: A thin, uniform-thickness plate formed as a left-right symmetric open lattice inscribed on a round bolt circle: a central rectangular bay carries an X diagonal brace, flanked by triangular gusset webs and side columns of parallel horizontal slats, with a small rectangular slot above and a trapezoidal opening below. Four rounded pad eyes on the bolt circle each take a small through hole, two edges are chamfered, and all ribs meet with small fillets and identical rib and gap widths.

family_pilot__Z_00043_0.desc: A uniform-thickness shouldered tag plate: a narrow outer rim with straight side edges and convex arched crown and foot surrounds one large through window with parallel sides, a flat header edge and a rounded lower edge. One round through-hole pierces the header above the window; outer and inner corners are filleted and the perimeter reads as a small chamfered or raised bead.
